redrawing then would only lose the picture.\n    if (nextRatio === ratio && nextWidth === width && nextHeight === height) return;\n    [ratio, width, height] = [nextRatio, nextWidth, nextHeight];\n    canvas.width = Math.round(width * ratio);\n    canvas.height = Math.round(height * ratio);\n    ctx.setTransform(ratio, 0, 0, ratio, 0, 0);\n    ctx.lineCap = 'round';\n    ctx.lineJoin = 'round';\n    const xs = columnsFor(width, o.grid);\n    columns = xs.map((x) => pace({ x, row: -Math.floor(random() * (height / cell()) * 1.5), tick: 0, code: o.pick() }));\n    if (!o.animate && o.visible) {\n      // A still field of symbols for people who prefer reduced motion.\n      for (let i = 0;                  |\n\n## 2. The rain scaled up too much (root cause)\n\nThe reported screenshot shows the rain glyphs and the stars blurred and several times too large. In Safari this happens on some loads only.\n\n**The cause.**\n\n- Both background canvases (the rain and the universe) took their size from CSS once, at start, and then only listened to the window `resize` event.\n- WebKit may run `<script type=\"module\">` before the stylesheet is applied ([WebKit bug 261655](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655)). At that moment a canvas still has the default size of 300×150 CSS pixels, so the bitmap is made 300 pixels wide.\n- When the stylesheet arrives, the canvas grows to the size of the window. The window itself did not change, so no `resize` event comes, and the 300-pixel bitmap is stretched over the screen: ×4.27 on a 1280-pixel window.\n- A refresh or a click on a menu item loads a new page, which is why it shows up there and not every time: the result depends on whether the cached stylesheet wins the race.\n\n**Reproduction.**\n\n- [`experiments/rain-scale.mjs`](../../../experiments/rain-scale.mjs) loads the built site in Chromium and, with `late`, attaches the stylesheet only after the scripts ran, as Safari does.\n- It prints the ratio between the CSS size and the bitmap of each canvas.\n- Before the fix the rain and the universe were \"stretched ×4.27\" on load, after a menu click and after a reload. After the fix the ratio is ×1.\n\n**The fix.**\n\n- [`src/visuals/size.js`](../../../src/visuals/size.js) adds `watchSize(element, onResize)`: a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas itself, plus the window `resize` event for changes of `devicePixelRatio`.\n- `rain.js` and `nebula.js` use it and skip redrawing when the size did not change, so the first report of the observer does not clear the picture.\n- `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` grows a canvas from 300×150 to the window size without a window event and checks that the bitmap follows.\n\n| Before (late stylesheet, ×4.27)                         | After (×1)                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Rain stretched](screenshots/rain-stretched-before.png) | ![Rain sharp](screenshots/rain-fixed-after.png)    |\n\n## 3. Settings\n\n![The settings page](screenshots/settings-page.png)\n\n**The store** ([`src/settings/`](../../../src/settings)):\n\n- `schema.js` describes 70 settings in 9 sections:\n\n  | Section                  | Settings |\n  | ------------------------ | -------- |\n  | Background animation     | 1        |\n  | Universe                 | 11       |\n  | Grid                     | 5        |\n  | Rain of link networks    | 14       |\n  | Skin                     | 1        |\n  | Glass                    | 4        |\n  | Liquid glass             | 16       |\n  | Futuristic               | 17       |\n  | Links theory notation    | 1        |\n\n- Every setting has a default, a range or a list of choices, and English and Russian labels.\n- `apply.js` checks the stored values (numbers are clamped, choices must be listed, colours must be `#rrggbb`). It puts them on `<html>`: numbers and colours become CSS variables, and switches and choices become `data-` attributes.\n- `store.js` saves only the values that differ from the defaults, in `localStorage` under `settings`. A better default chosen later still reaches everyone who did not change that setting. Other open tabs follow through the `storage` event.\n- The same check and apply code is inlined into a script that runs before the first paint (`vite.config.js`), so a chosen skin never flashes the default one.\n\n**The page** `/settings/`:\n\n- It is linked from the footer of every page.\n- Every change is applied at once: the page itself and its background are the preview.\n- The universe, the grid and the rain read the settings while they run, so nothing restarts.\n- \"Look at the background\" hides the page for a moment.\n- Reset works for a single setting, a section or everything.\n- The changes can be copied as JSON and loaded back, to send a set of defaults.\n\n**Choices.**\n\n- The defaults are exactly the values the site used before. Nothing changes for a visitor until they change something.\n- Settings are per browser, and the page says so.\n\n## 4. Skins\n\n`skin.name` is `glass` (the existing skin and the default), `liquid` or `futuristic`. The glass skin's opacity, blur, bar and radius became settings too.\n\n**Liquid glass** ([`src/skins.liquid.css`](../../../src/skins.liquid.css)) has 16 settings:\n\n- blur, saturation, brightness, tint colour and level, radius;\n- light on the edges, edge width, depth, shadow and sheen;\n- floating panels and capsule buttons;\n- refraction through an SVG displacement filter ([`LiquidRefraction.jsx`](../../../src/components/LiquidRefraction.jsx)), with its strength and detail. The filter works only where `backdrop-filter: url()` is supported (Chromium). Other browsers keep the blur.\n\n| Dark                                          | Light                                           |\n| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Liquid dark](screenshots/skin-liquid-dark.png) | ![Liquid light](screenshots/skin-liquid-light.png) |\n\n**Futuristic** ([`src/skins.future.css`](../../../src/skins.future.css), [`src/skins.palettes.css`](../../../src/skins.palettes.css)) follows the HUD style of konard/immortality. It has 17 settings:\n\n- 12 palettes: mission, tron, ares, clu, athena, aphrodite, poseidon, soulextract, glitchy, amber, matrix and monochrome (contrast checked by `experiments/future-palettes.mjs`);\n- 8 frames: corners, chamfer, octagon, kranox, bracket, lines, underline and plain, with the cut and corner sizes;\n- 9 surfaces: gradient, glass, frosted, solid, transparent, steel, carbon, holographic and blueprint, with opacity and blur;\n- border, accent bar, glow, display and body fonts, letter case, spacing, title style, hover effect and scanlines.\n\n| Dark                                             | Light                                              | Settings                                                 |\n| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Futuristic dark](screenshots/skin-future-dark.png) | ![Futuristic light](screenshots/skin-future-light.png) | ![Futuristic settings](screenshots/skin-future-settings.png) |\n\nThe frames chamfer, octagon, kranox and bracket are in `screenshots/skin-future-*.png`.\n\n## 5. Only real references\n\nA network of N links writes each link as a source and a target. With the zero link (\"nothing\"), each of the 2N digits is one of 0…N: (N+1)^(2N) networks. With only real references, the digits are 1…N: N^(2N) networks.\n\n| Links | Default (with 0) | Only real references |\n| ----- | ---------------- | -------------------- |\n| 1     | 4                | 1                    |\n| 2     | 81               | 16                   |\n| 3     | 4,096            | 729                  |\n| 4     | 390,625          | 65,536               |\n\n- `codeAt`, `networkCount`, `classCount` and `representatives` in `src/links/configurations.js` take `{ real }`. The i-th real network is computed directly, without filtering.\n- The button sits next to \"One per renaming\" and works with it. It is off by default.\n- The rain can also use only real networks (`rain.real`, off by default).\n\n| Default, 2 links (81)                                 | Only real references, 2 links (16)                 |\n| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Default gallery](screenshots/gallery-default.png)   | ![Real references](screenshots/gallery-real.png)   |\n\n## 6.                  |\n\n## 2. The rain scaled up too much (root cause)\n\nThe reported screenshot shows the rain glyphs and the stars blurred and several times too large. In Safari this happens on some loads only.\n\n**The cause.**\n\n- Both background canvases (the rain and the universe) took their size from CSS once, at start, and then only listened to the window `resize` event.\n- WebKit may run `<script type=\"module\">` before the stylesheet is applied ([WebKit bug 261655](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655)). At that moment a canvas still has the default size of 300×150 CSS pixels, so the bitmap is made 300 pixels wide.\n- When the stylesheet arrives, the canvas grows to the size of the window. The window itself did not change, so no `resize` event comes, and the 300-pixel bitmap is stretched over the screen: ×4.27 on a 1280-pixel window.\n- A refresh or a click on a menu item loads a new page, which is why it shows up there and not every time: the result depends on whether the cached stylesheet wins the race.\n\n**Reproduction.**\n\n- [`experiments/rain-scale.mjs`](../../../experiments/rain-scale.mjs) loads the built site in Chromium and, with `late`, attaches the stylesheet only after the scripts ran, as Safari does.\n- It prints the ratio between the CSS size and the bitmap of each canvas.\n- Before the fix the rain and the universe were \"stretched ×4.27\" on load, after a menu click and after a reload. After the fix the ratio is ×1.\n\n**The fix.**\n\n- [`src/visuals/size.js`](../../../src/visuals/size.js) adds `watchSize(element, onResize)`: a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas itself, plus the window `resize` event for changes of `devicePixelRatio`.\n- `rain.js` and `nebula.js` use it and skip redrawing when the size did not change, so the first report of the observer does not clear the picture.\n- `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` grows a canvas from 300×150 to the window size without a window event and checks that the bitmap follows.\n\n| Before (late stylesheet, ×4.27)                         | After (×1)                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Rain stretched](screenshots/rain-stretched-before.png) | ![Rain sharp](screenshots/rain-fixed-after.png)    |\n\n## 3. Settings\n\n![The settings page](screenshots/settings-page.png)\n\n**The store** ([`src/settings/`](../../../src/settings)):\n\n- `schema.js` describes 70 settings in 9 sections:\n\n  | Section                  | Settings |\n  | ------------------------ | -------- |\n  | Background animation     | 1        |\n  | Universe                 | 11       |\n  | Grid                     | 5        |\n  | Rain of link networks    | 14       |\n  | Skin                     | 1        |\n  | Glass                    | 4        |\n  | Liquid glass             | 16       |\n  | Futuristic               | 17       |\n  | Links theory notation    | 1        |\n\n- Every setting has a default, a range or a list of choices, and English and Russian labels.\n- `apply.js` checks the stored values (numbers are clamped, choices must be listed, colours must be `#rrggbb`). It puts them on `<html>`: numbers and colours become CSS variables, and switches and choices become `data-` attributes.\n- `store.js` saves only the values that differ from the defaults, in `localStorage` under `settings`. A better default chosen later still reaches everyone who did not change that setting. Other open tabs follow through the `storage` event.\n- The same check and apply code is inlined into a script that runs before the first paint (`vite.config.js`), so a chosen skin never flashes the default one.\n\n**The page** `/settings/`:\n\n- It is linked from the footer of every page.\n- Every change is applied at once: the page itself and its background are the preview.\n- The universe, the grid and the rain read the settings while they run, so nothing restarts.\n- \"Look at the background\" hides the page for a moment.\n- Reset works for a single setting, a section or everything.\n- The changes can be copied as JSON and loaded back, to send a set of defaults.\n\n**Choices.**\n\n- The defaults are exactly the values the site used before. Nothing changes for a visitor until they change something.\n- Settings are per browser, and the page says so.\n\n## 4. Skins\n\n`skin.name` is `glass` (the existing skin and the default), `liquid` or `futuristic`. The glass skin's opacity, blur, bar and radius became settings too.\n\n**Liquid glass** ([`src/skins.liquid.css`](../../../src/skins.liquid.css)) has 16 settings:\n\n- blur, saturation, brightness, tint colour and level, radius;\n- light on the edges, edge width, depth, shadow and sheen;\n- floating panels and capsule buttons;\n- refraction through an SVG displacement filter ([`LiquidRefraction.jsx`](../../../src/components/LiquidRefraction.jsx)), with its strength and detail. The filter works only where `backdrop-filter: url()` is supported (Chromium). Other browsers keep the blur.\n\n| Dark                                          | Light                                           |\n| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Liquid dark](screenshots/skin-liquid-dark.png) | ![Liquid light](screenshots/skin-liquid-light.png) |\n\n**Futuristic** ([`src/skins.future.css`](../../../src/skins.future.css), [`src/skins.palettes.css`](../../../src/skins.palettes.css)) follows the HUD style of konard/immortality. [2026-10-23T16:18:33.917Z] [INFO]         "content": "## `corner-shape` summary\n\n**Purpose:** A shorthand that sets the shape of a box's corners within the area defined by `border-radius`. Borders, outlines, shadows, backgrounds, and overflow follow the shape. Without a non-zero `border-radius`, it has no effect.\n\n### Values\n\nEach value is a `<corner-shape-value>`: a keyword or a `superellipse()` function. Keywords map to specific `superellipse()` values:\n\n| Keyword | Equivalent |\n|---|---|\n| `square` | `superellipse(infinity)` |\n| `squircle` | `superellipse(2)` |\n| `round` | `superellipse(1)` (initial value; same as `border-radius` alone) |\n| `bevel` | `superellipse(0)` |\n| `scoop` | `superellipse(-1)` |\n| `notch` | `superellipse(-infinity)` |\n\n`superellipse()` takes a `<number>`, `infinity`, or `-infinity`.\n\n### Shorthand syntax\n\nThe shorthand accepts one to four values, following the same pattern as margin and padding:\n\n- **1 value:** all four corners\n- **2 values:** top-left and bottom-right, then top-right and bottom-left\n- **3 values:** top-left, then top-right and bottom-left, then bottom-right\n- **4 values:** top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left (clockwise)\n\n```css\ncorner-shape: bevel;\ncorner-shape: notch superellipse(0.6);\ncorner-shape: superellipse(-1.2) square squircle;\ncorner-shape: scoop superellipse(-1.6) superellipse(-2.2) round;\n```\n\n### Longhands\n\n**Per-corner, physical:**\n- `corner-top-left-shape`\n- `corner-top-right-shape`\n- `corner-bottom-left-shape`\n- `corner-bottom-right-shape`\n\n**Per-corner, logical:**\n- `corner-start-start-shape`\n- `corner-start-end-shape`\n- `corner-end-start-shape`\n- `corner-end-end-shape`\n\n**Side shorthands (two corners each), physical:**\n- `corner-top-shape`, `corner-right-shape`, `corner-bottom-shape`, `corner-left-shape`\n\n**Side shorthands, logical:**\n- `corner-block-start-shape`, `corner-block-end-shape`, `corner-inline-start-shape`, `corner-inline-end-shape`\n\n### Other notes\n\n- **Animation:** Keyword values interpolate through their `superellipse()` equivalents, so transitions and keyframe animations between shapes are smooth.\n- **Constraint:** If opposite corners overlap (for example, large `border-radius` values with `scoop`), the browser reduces the radii to prevent overlap.\n- **`border-shape` conflict:** `corner-shape` has no effect when `border-shape` is set, because `border-shape` ignores `border-radius`.\n\n### Specification\n\n[CSS Borders and Box Decorations Module Level RESOLVED FIXED 314536 [GTK][WPE] Skia Compositor: wrong layer position for the combination of backdrop-filter and clip-path\n- **Background on composited layers in columns:** Bug 120436 (2013) moved compositing layers into the correct column by adjusting coordinate conversion, replacing an older hack that had broken hit-testing. The old hack in RenderLayer::updateLayerPosition() for placing layers in columns changed the layer position for composited layers, which broke hit-testing. The fix moves compositing layers to the correct positions by applying column offsets in convertToLayerCoords().\n- **Why composited layers resist splitting:** An older WebKit ChangeLog states that composited layers remain unsplittable and have a hacked offset still in order to be placed in the right column.\n- **Backdrop-filter sizing in WebKit:** Bug 145561 changed the backdrop filter layer to take its size and position from its renderer rather than the composited layer, since the composited bounds could expand for box shadows or absolutely positioned descendants. The backdrop filter layer should take its size and position from its renderer and not directly from the composited layer.\n- **Filters and fragmentation (Chromium):** A Chromium change notes that filter effects are set up before fragmentation, so their bounding box has to be converted out of flow-thread coordinates manually. This is not the case for filters. They are set up before fragmentation. Therefore, we need to make the bounding box of the layer visual (convert out of the flow thread coordinate space) on our own.\n- **Known limitation in Chromium:** A 2019 Chromium commit says fragmentation of composited layers isn't allowed, and the fragment clip is skipped for them. It adds that the result is still not fully correct, though less broken in many cases.\n\nSuggested next step: search WebKit Bugzilla directly for \"backdrop-filter multicol\" or \"composited column\" to find a bug that covers this exact case, since a direct match wasn't in these results.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."

Wider than the viewport means something overflowed.. It also reports a tolerance of about 1px to absorb rounding.\n- **Hidden overflow evades it.** That same project notes that when an ancestor uses overflow-x: hidden, the content is clipped rather than scrolled, so scrollWidth doesn't change and the test passes even though text is cut off. It recommends comparing those elements against the box of whatever clips them (scrollWidth never moves and the page passes while text is cut off).\n- **Playwright implementation.** A Playwright-based example in a Python test suite runs the check at a 375px viewport on each public route and asserts that the body's scroll width doesn't exceed the viewport width (Tests verify: No horizontal overflow (scrollWidth > clientWidth) at 375px viewport). A TypeScript utility from another source returns a structured result with the overflow amount and the offending elements.\n- **Per-element scans.** Some write-ups run a per-element scan in the page rather than relying on the document-level value. One suggests filtering all elements where scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth, and warns that you have to remember to run it at every breakpoint (The problem: you have to remember to run it, at the right width, for every breakpoint.).\n- **Measurement caveat.** MDN's documentation (in German) explains that scrollWidth includes padding but excludes margins and any vertical scrollbar, and that it equals clientWidth when nothing overflows.\n- **Gotcha.** A Django ticket shows a test that used misspelled properties (scrollWeight / offsetWeight), so the check silently never fired. Verify that a deliberately overflowing fixture fails the test.\n\nA minimal Playwright version would set the viewport, load the page, and assert that `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= document.documentElement.clientWidth + tolerance`. Then add the per-element scan for diagnostics and a clipping check for overflow: hidden. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - Stack: React 19 + Vite 8 multi-page app, tested with Vitest + jsdom.\n   - Checks:\n     - `npm run check` runs eslint, prettier, the file line limit (1500 max outside docs/ and dev/) and secretlint.\n     - A husky pre-commit hook runs lint-staged.\n   - Settings helpers live in src/settings/fields.js: `range(key,d,min,max,step,label,extra)`, `toggle`, `select`, `color`, `option(value,en,ru)`.\n     - `extra` can carry `unit`, `hint`, `css:false`, `when(settings)` and `tab`.\n   - Sections have `id`, `title`, `lead`, `when` and `column` (1 by default). They may also have `tabs: [{id,on,label}]`.\n   - normalize and applySettings in apply.js are ES5 and are stringified into SETTINGS_SCRIPT.\n   - How settings reach CSS:\n     - Numbers and colours become `--a-b-c` CSS variables. The unit is appended unless it is % or ×, so percent values are bare numbers and must be used as `calc(x/100)`.\n     - Toggles and selects become `data-a-b-c` attributes on `<html>`.\n   - New this session:\n     - `CSS_RULES` is the subset of RULES whose fields have `css !== false`. It is used by store.apply and SETTINGS_SCRIPT, while normalize still uses the full RULES.\n     - Only the new JS-only fields are css:false. Existing fields keep their CSS vars, because a test checks `--rain-step`.\n   - Background layer order, bottom to top:\n     1. `.cosmos__universe` (WebGL);\n     2. `.cosmos__stars` (Canvas2D, lazily imported);\n     3. `.cosmos__grid` (CSS);\n     4. `.cosmos__beams` (Canvas2D, lazy; same top offset and drift as the grid);\n     5. `.cosmos__rain`.\n   - Headless shots use experiments/settings-shot.mjs (`ENGINE=webkit|firefox`). The vite preview runs on port 4173; rebuild with `npm run build` first.\n\n3. audio.sampleRate);\n    const data = noiseBuffer.getChannelData(0);\n    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;\n  }\n  return noiseBuffer;\n}\n\n/** A short stereo room: decaying, slightly low-passed noise. */\nfunction roomImpulse(audio, seconds) {\n  const length = Math.ceil(audio.sampleRate * seconds);\n  const buffer = audio.createBuffer(2, length, audio.sampleRate);\n  for (let channel = 0; channel < 2; channel++) {\n    const data = buffer.getChannelData(channel);\n    let last = 0;\n    for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {\n      last = last * start, voice, gain) {\n  const amp = audio.createGain();\n  const attack = Math.min(voice.attack ?? 0.004, voice.duration * 0.8);\n  amp.gain.setValueAtTime(0, start);\n node = node.connect(panner);\n      }\n      node.connect(output);\n    }\n  }\n  return end;\n}\n\n/**\n * Which of the sounds of an interaction play: one at random (never the\n * `previous` one The AudioContext is made\n// only after the visitor has interacted with the page, so browsers never warn\n// about autoplay, and only when sound is switched on (this module is loaded\n// only then, audio.sampleRate);\n    const data = noiseBuffer.getChannelData(0);\n    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;\n  }\n  return noiseBuffer;\n}\n\n/** A short stereo room: decaying, slightly low-passed noise. */\nfunction roomImpulse(audio, seconds) {\n  const length = Math.ceil(audio.sampleRate * seconds);\n  const buffer = audio.createBuffer(2, length, audio.sampleRate);\n  for (let channel = 0; channel < 2; channel++) {\n    const data = buffer.getChannelData(channel);\n    let last = 0;\n    for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {\n      last = last * compressor.knee.value = 12;\n  compressor.ratio.value = 4;\n  compressor.attack.value = 0.003;\n  compressor.release.value = 0.15;\n  const convolver = audio.createConvolver();\n  convolver.buffer = compressor.connect(destination);\n  return { input, shelf, wet, convolver, compressor };\n}\n\n/** An attack and decay that releases to true silence, without clicks. */\nfunction envelope(audio, amp.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.00011, gain), start + attack);\n  amp.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, start + voice.duration);\n  amp.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0, start + Key Technical Concepts:\n   - Stack: React 19 + Vite 8 multi-page app; Vitest + jsdom.\n     - Tests are `src/**/*.test.{js,jsx}`; Node `fs` works in tests.\n     - setupTests resets settings after each test.\n   - `npm run check` runs eslint, prettier --check, the 1500-line limit and secretlint. Husky lint-staged runs on commit.\n   - Schema helpers (fields.js): `range`, `toggle`, `select`, `color`, `option`.\n     - `extra` keys: `unit`, `hint`, `css:false`, `when(s)`, `tab`, `tiles`, plus the new `preview:'sound'`.\n     - Sections have `id`, `title`, `lead`, `when`, `column` (default 1) and `tabs`.\n   - applySettings:\n     - numbers and colours become CSS variables;\n     - selects and toggles become `data-` attributes;\n     - fields with `css:false` are not put on <html>.\n   - formatValue:\n     - unit '%' with max ≤ 2 shows as a percent;\n     - '%', '×' and '°' are appended without a space;\n     - any other unit gets a space (\"15 cents\", \"1.4 s\", \"80 ms\").\n   - applied.test.js requires every field to be used by CSS, by a layer option builder (`readByLayers` spies on nebulaOptions, starsOptions, beamsOptions and rainOptions), or by a script that contains the literal `'key'` (schema files excluded).\n   - Lazy loading pattern: Cosmos `useLazyLayer` with `import()`.\n   - Screenshot tools need `npm run build`; the preview runs on port 4173:\n     - `node experiments/settings-shot.mjs <path> '<json>' <out.png> [light|dark] [scroll|full] [width]`;\n     - `node experiments/corner-zoom.mjs <path> '<json>' <selector> <out.png> [light|dark]`.\n\n3. **New, uncommitted, step F:**\n     - **src/sound/library.js**: `SOUND_SPECS` holds 31 patches.\n       - 26 are ported from immortality: quartz, cobalt, comet, ion, halo, tide, mica, nova, zephyr, ember, prism, glacier, pulsar, orbit, vapor, cinder, tungsten, helix, drift, basalt, flint, opal, lumen, sonar, vesper, relay.\n       - 5 are new: raindrop, link, glass, warp, byte.\n       - Helpers: `tone(wave, from, to, duration, gain, extra)`, `noise(type, from, to, duration, gain, {q, ...})`, `lowpass(from, to=from, q)`.\n     - **src/sound/engine.js**:\n       - Exports `TONE_SHELF={warm:-7,neutral:0,bright:5}`.\n       - `createBus(audio, destination, {room=1.4})` returns `{input, shelf, wet, convolver, compressor}`.\n       - `playSpec(spec, audio, output, {gain, detune, pan, at})` returns the end time.\n       - `chooseSounds(list, mode, turn, random, previous)` implements random (no repeat of the previous pick), cycle and layer.\n       - `createPlayer(options, {Audio=globalThis.AudioContext, random})` returns `{configure(next), setPan, play(id, gain), trigger(event), suspend, close}`.\n         - `configure` rebuilds the convolver buffer when `room` changes.\n         - The AudioContext is created lazily and only if `navigator.userActivation` has been active.\n         - `trigger` uses `current.effects[event]` and gain `levels[event]/sqrt(n)`, and returns the ids played.\n         - `play` applies detune `pitch` cents, ±10% level humanization, and pan `pan*width` when stereo is on.\n     - **src/sound/options.js**:\n       - `soundOptions(s)` returns `{on, volume, mode, tone, reverb, room, pitch, stereo, width, gap, effects:{event:[ids up to the first 'none']}, levels:{event: s['sound.<event>Level']}}`.\n       - `CUE='site:sound'`.\n       - `cue(event)` dispatches a CustomEvent on window.\n     - **src/sound/interactions.js**:\n       - `clickEvent(element)`:\n         - summary → null (the details toggle sounds it);\n         - checkbox → toggle; radio → select;\n         - role tab/radio → select;\n         - aria-pressed → toggle;\n         - everything else → activate.\n       - `startSound(options, {player=createPlayer(options), now})` returns `{update, preview(id), play(event, gap), stop}`.\n       - Its listeners are capture + passive on document:\n         - pointermove: sets the pan; scans `[data-tooltip-root]` at most every 90 ms;\n         - pointerover: hover on INTERACTIVE elements; skips touch and pen; throttled by `current.gap`;\n         - click;\n         - input: a range input fires select (70 ms); text fields fire type (30 ms);\n         - change: select and color inputs fire select;\n         - toggle: details open/close;\n         - window CUE: plays the cued event;\n         - visibilitychange: suspends when hidden.\n     - **src/settings/schema.sound.js**:\n       - `SOUNDS` is an array of `[id, en, enCharacter, ru, ruCharacter]` (31 entries); `SOUND_IDS`.\n       - `SOUND_OPTIONS` is 'none' plus the sounds.\n       - `SOUND_EVENTS` is `[id, en, ru, defaults]`:\n         - hover [quartz], activate [cobalt, relay], toggle [flint], select [comet], scan [ion];\n         - open [zephyr], close [vapor], type [], intro [nova] (\"Switching the sound on\"), notify [lumen].\n       - `SOUND_SLOTS=[1,2,3,4]`.\n       - `SOUND_SECTION` (id 'sound', column 1 by default). Every field is `css:false`, and every field except `sound.on` has `when: on`.\n         - General fields:\n           - `sound.on` (false);\n           - `sound.volume` (0–2, d 1, %);\n           - `sound.mode` (random/cycle/layer);\n           - `sound.tone` (warm/neutral/bright);\n           - `sound.reverb` (0–1, d 0.2, %);\n           - `sound.room` (0.3–4 s, d 1.4, shown when reverb > 0);\n           - `sound.pitch` (0–100, d 15, 'cents');\n           - `sound.stereo` (true);\n           - `sound.width` (0–1, d 0.6, %, shown when stereo is on);\n           - `sound.gap` (0–500 ms, d 80).\n         - Per event:\n           - `sound.<event>1..4`: selects with `preview:'sound'`; slot n is shown only when the previous slots are not 'none';\n           - `sound.<event>Level` (0–2, %): shown when slot 1 is not 'none'.\n     - **src/components/Sound.jsx**:\n       - lazy `import('../sound/interactions')`;\n       - a module-level `session`;\n       - exports `previewSound(id)`;\n       - the default component `Sound()` starts or stops the session when `sound.on` changes and calls `session.update(soundOptions(settings))` on every change; it plays 'intro' only when the visitor switches sound on, not on mount.\n\n   - **Edited, uncommitted:**\n     - src/settings/schema.js: imports SOUND_SECTION, puts it after `rain` in SECTIONS, and updates the comment.\n     - src/components/Layout.jsx: imports Sound and renders `<Sound />` after `<LiquidRefraction />`.\n     - src/components/PrefSwitches.jsx:\n       - imports setSettings and useSettings;\n       - adds a `prefs__sound` button with aria-pressed={sound} and aria-label \"Sounds of the interface\";\n       - its title is \"Sound: on/off\";\n       - it draws an SVG speaker with waves, or an X when sound is off;\n       - clicking it toggles `sound.on`.\n     - src/Layout.css: `.prefs__theme, .prefs__sound` share the round style; 0.55 + (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * 0.45;\n      data[i] = last * Math.pow(1 - i / length, 3.2);\n    }\n  }\n  return buffer;\n}\n\n/** The master chain on `audio`: input → tone shelf → compressor → destination, with a reverb send. */\nexport function createBus(audio, destination = audio.destination, { room = 1.4 } = {}) {\n  const input = audio.createGain();\n  const shelf = audio.createBiquadFilter();\n  shelf.type = 'highshelf';\n  shelf.frequency.value = 3200;\n  const compressor = audio.createDynamicsCompressor();\n  compressor.threshold.value = -18;\n  compressor.knee.value = 12;\n  compressor.ratio.value = 4;\n  compressor.attack.value = 0.003;\n  compressor.release.value = 0.15;\n  const convolver = audio.createConvolver();\n  convolver.buffer = roomImpulse(audio, room);\n  const wet = audio.createGain();\n  input.connect(shelf);\n  shelf.connect(compressor);\n  shelf.connect(convolver);\n  convolver.connect(wet).connect(compressor);\n  compressor.connect(destination);\n  return { input, shelf, wet, convolver, compressor };\n}\n\n/** An attack and decay that releases to true silence, without clicks. */\nfunction envelope(audio, start, voice, gain) {\n  const amp = audio.createGain();\n  const attack = Math.min(voice.attack ?? 0.004, voice.duration * 0.8);\n  amp.gain.setValueAtTime(0, start);\n  amp.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.00011, gain), start + attack);\n  amp.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, start + voice.duration);\n  amp.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0, start + voice.duration + 0.01);\n  return amp;\n}\n\nfunction sweep(param, value, start, duration) {\n  param.setValueAtTime(value.from, start);\n  if (value.to !== value.from) param.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(1, value.to), start + duration);\n}\n\n/**\n * Schedules the patch `spec` on `audio` into `output`; returns when it ends.\n * `gain` scales it, `detune` (cents) shifts it, `pan` (−1…1) moves it.\n */\nexport function playSpec(spec, audio, output, { gain = 1, detune = 0, pan = 0, at = audio.currentTime } = {}) {\n  let end = at;\n  for (let r = 0; r < (spec.repeat ?? 1); r++) {\n    const repeatGain = gain * Math.pow(spec.repeatDecay ?? 1, r);\n    for (const voice of spec.voices) {\n      const start = at + r * (spec.gap ?? 0) + (voice.delay ?? mod.connect(depth).connect(source.frequency);\n          mod.start(start);\n          mod.stop(stop);\n        }\n        source.start(start);\n      }\n      source.stop(stop);\n      let node =  const more = [];\n  if (list.scrollLeft > 1) more.push('left');\n  if (list.scrollLeft + list.clientWidth < list.scrollWidth - 1) more.push('right');\n  if (more.length) list.dataset.more = more.join(' ');\n  else delete list.dataset.more;\n}\n\n/** Scrolls a list sideways so that its current link is in the middle. */\nexport function centreCurrent(list) {\n  const current = list.querySelector('[aria-current=\"page\"]');\n  if (!current || list.scrollWidth <= list.clientWidth) return;\n  const [box, link] = [list.getBoundingClientRect(), current.getBoundingClientRect()];\n  list.scrollLeft += link.left - box.left - (box.width - link.width) / 2;\n}\n\n/** Keeps the edges of the lists marked while they scroll and the window resizes; returns the cleanup. */\nexport function watchEdges(lists) {\n  const update = () => lists.forEach(markEdges);\n  update();\n  lists.forEach((list) => list.addEventListener('scroll', update, { passive: true }));\n  window.addEventListener('resize', update);\n  return () => {\n    lists.forEach((list) => list.removeEventListener('scroll', update));\n    window.removeEventListener('resize', The rain scaled up too much (root cause)\n\nThe reported screenshot shows the rain glyphs and the stars blurred and several times too large. In Safari this happens on some loads only.\n\n**The cause.**\n\n- Both background canvases (the rain and the universe) took their size from CSS once, at start, and then only listened to the window `resize` event.\n- WebKit may run `<script type=\"module\">` before the stylesheet is applied ([WebKit bug 261655](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655)). At that moment a canvas still has the default size of 300×150 CSS pixels, so the bitmap is made 300 pixels wide.\n- When the stylesheet arrives, the canvas grows to the size of the window. The window itself did not change, so no `resize` event comes, and the 300-pixel bitmap is stretched over the screen: ×4.27 on a 1280-pixel window.\n- A refresh or a click on a menu item loads a new page, which is why it shows up there and not every time: the result depends on whether the cached stylesheet wins the race.\n\n**Reproduction.**\n\n- [`experiments/rain-scale.mjs`](../../../experiments/rain-scale.mjs) loads the built site in Chromium and, with `late`, attaches the stylesheet only after the scripts ran, as Safari does.\n- It prints the ratio between the CSS size and the bitmap of each canvas.\n- Before the fix the rain and the universe were \"stretched ×4.27\" on load, after a menu click and after a reload. After the fix the ratio is ×1.\n\n**The fix.**\n\n- [`src/visuals/size.js`](../../../src/visuals/size.js) adds `watchSize(element, onResize)`: a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas itself, plus the window `resize` event for changes of `devicePixelRatio`.\n- `rain.js` and `nebula.js` use it and skip redrawing when the size did not change, so the first report of the observer does not clear the picture.\n- `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` grows a canvas from 300×150 to the window size without a window event and checks that the bitmap follows.\n\n| Before (late stylesheet, ×4.27)                         | After (×1)                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |",

The rain scaled up too much (root cause)\n\nThe reported screenshot shows the rain glyphs and the stars blurred and several times too large. In Safari this happens on some loads only.\n\n**The cause.**\n\n- Both background canvases (the rain and the universe) took their size from CSS once, at start, and then only listened to the window `resize` event.\n- WebKit may run `<script type=\"module\">` before the stylesheet is applied ([WebKit bug 261655](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655)). At that moment a canvas still has the default size of 300×150 CSS pixels, so the bitmap is made 300 pixels wide.\n- When the stylesheet arrives, the canvas grows to the size of the window. The window itself did not change, so no `resize` event comes, and the 300-pixel bitmap is stretched over the screen: ×4.27 on a 1280-pixel window.\n- A refresh or a click on a menu item loads a new page, which is why it shows up there and not every time: the result depends on whether the cached stylesheet wins the race.\n\n**Reproduction.**\n\n- [`experiments/rain-scale.mjs`](../../../experiments/rain-scale.mjs) loads the built site in Chromium and, with `late`, attaches the stylesheet only after the scripts ran, as Safari does.\n- It prints the ratio between the CSS size and the bitmap of each canvas.\n- Before the fix the rain and the universe were \"stretched ×4.27\" on load, after a menu click and after a reload. After the fix the ratio is ×1.\n\n**The fix.**\n\n- [`src/visuals/size.js`](../../../src/visuals/size.js) adds `watchSize(element, onResize)`: a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas itself, plus the window `resize` event for changes of `devicePixelRatio`.\n- `rain.js` and `nebula.js` use it and skip redrawing when the size did not change, so the first report of the observer does not clear the picture.\n- `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` grows a canvas from 300×150 to the window size without a window event and checks that the bitmap follows.\n\n| Before (late stylesheet, ×4.27)                         | After (×1)                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |\n230 docs/case-studies/issue-13/README.md",

                                                                             |\n\nThe commits of the pull request follow the same order: defaults → settings layout → glass → background → frames → sound → presets → phones → this case study.\n\n## 2. The new defaults, and \"all settings are actually applied\"\n\n**The defaults.** The 21 values of the issue are now the defaults: `nebula.*`, `grid.size`, `grid.period`, `rain.*` and `glass.*`. `src/settings/settings.test.js` holds the JSON of the issue as it was given. It checks that every key exists and that `DEFAULTS` equal it.\n\n**The check.** A default that nothing reads looks like it works, but changing it does nothing. There are three ways a setting reaches the page:\n\n- `apply.js` writes it as a CSS variable or an attribute of `<html>`, and a stylesheet uses it;\n- the background scripts read it as an option (the nebula, stars, beams and rain);\n- a component reads its key (the sound, the skins).\n\n[`src/settings/applied.test.js`](../../../src/settings/applied.test.js) goes through all 251 settings:\n\n- It reads every stylesheet and script of `src/`, leaving out the schema and the tests.\n- It runs the option builders of the background layers and of the sound through a `Proxy`, which records every key they read.\n- It fails for any setting that is not used in one of the three ways.\n- It also checks itself: an invented `nebula.unread` must be reported, and a real `rain.step` must not.\n- A second test checks every choice of every select: a choice must have a CSS rule for `[data-…='value']` or be read by a script. Choices that switch something off (`none`, `plain`) need no rule.\n\n## 3. Space around rain symbols, and the rain glow on Retina screens\n\n- `rain.padding` adds space around every symbol, from 0 to 24 pixels, so columns and rows keep their distance. [`src/visuals/rain.js`](../../../src/visuals/rain.js) adds it to the cell of a symbol.\n- While checking the rain settings on a 2× screen, the glow turned out to be half as large as on a 1× screen. `shadowBlur` is in canvas pixels, not CSS pixels, so the glow is now multiplied by the device pixel ratio, like the font size already was. `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` checks the glow at ×1 and ×2.\n\n## 4. The Skin block jumped and was misaligned (root cause)\n\nThe fourth screenshot of the issue shows the Skin section in the wrong column, with the tops of the columns uneven.\n\n**The cause.**\n\n- The settings page laid out its sections with CSS multi-column (`columns: 2`). The browser balances the columns by height, so the column of a section depends on the height of every section before it.\n- The skin sections (glass, liquid, futuristic) have different heights. With glass, Rain was in the second column; with liquid and futuristic, it was in the first. So choosing another skin moved Rain to the other column, and every section after it moved too. Skin is one of those sections, so it \"disappeared\" from where the user had been looking.\n- In WebKit it was worse: every section ended up in one column, and the tops of the columns were negative (−365 px and −579 px).\n\n**Reproduction.** [`experiments/settings-layout.mjs`](../../../experiments/settings-layout.mjs) opens the settings page in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with each skin. It prints the column of each section, the tops of the columns, and the sections that change their column between glass and liquid. The logs are in `data/`:\n\n- [`layout-before-chromium.log`](data/layout-before-chromium.log): \"sections that change their column between glass and liquid: rain\".\n- [`layout-before-webkit.log`](data/layout-before-webkit.log): one column, tops −365 and −579.\n- [`layout-after-chromium.log`](data/layout-after-chromium.log), [`-firefox`](data/layout-after-firefox.log), [`-webkit`](data/layout-after-webkit.log): the same two columns in every browser and for every skin; tops equal; \"none\".\n\n**The fix.**\n\n- The page now has two fixed columns: motion, universe, grid, rain and share on the left; skin, the chosen skin, and theory on the right. A section never changes its column.\n- Every row is one grid of label | control | value | reset, so controls and values line up across sections.\n- The settings shared by all tabs (sound, motion) come before the tabs.\n\n| Before, glass (Chromium)                                         | Before, liquid: Rain moved to the left                              | After, liquid                                                      |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| ![Before glass](screenshots/settings-before-chromium-glass.png)  | ![Before liquid](screenshots/settings-before-chromium-liquid.png)   | ![After liquid](screenshots/settings-after-chromium-liquid.png)    |\n\n| Before, WebKit (one column)                               | After, WebKit                                           |\n| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Before WebKit](screenshots/settings-before-webkit.png)  | ![After WebKit](screenshots/settings-after-webkit.png)  |\n\n## 5. Polish: the glass skin\n\nTwo problems turned up while checking all panels with the glass skin:\n\n- **Blue panels.** The saturation of the backdrop was a percent written as a plain number, so `saturate(100)` (×100, not 100%) painted the panels blue. Values above 2 are now divided by 100, and a test covers it.\n- **Panels without blur.** Page cards, Habr cards, the language cloud and the theory panels had no blur. One rule now gives every panel the blur and the corner radius.\n\nWhere the look is a matter of taste, it got its own setting rather than a fixed choice: the colour behind panels, borders and lines, the shadow, and the light on the upper edge.\n\n| Dark                                                  | Light                                                   |\n| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Glass dark](screenshots/glass-options-dark.png)     | ![Glass light](screenshots/glass-options-light.png)     |\n\n## 6. Background: levels and every layer\n\nThe background has five layers, from back to front. Each has a strength from 0 to 100%, and 0 also stops its work.\n\n| Layer      | Settings                                                                                                                                                          |\n| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Universe   | strength, speed, gas, hue and colours, zoom, its own stars (amount, size, brightness, twinkling), vignette                                                         |\n| Star layers (1–4) | count of layers; for each: amount, **shape** (12), size and spread of sizes, colour and second colour, **glow** and glow colour, twinkling, spin, drift and its angle, warp and orbit, trails, blending |\n| Beams      | the \"effects that go vertically and horizontally\": light running along the grid lines; amount, direction (horizontal, vertical, both), speed, length, width, colour, glow |\n| Grid       | strength, size, period, **style** (lines, dashes, crosses, dots), colour                                                                                          |\n| Rain       | strength, step, speeds, density, fade, line width, glow and glow colour, padding                                                                                  |\n\n- The 12 star shapes are dot, soft, ring, square, diamond, cross, x, star4, star5, star6, sparkle and flare.\n- [`src/visuals/stars.js`](../../../src/visuals/stars.js) draws each shape once into a sprite for its size, colour and glow, then stamps the sprites. A frame of 4 layers costs no more path drawing than one.\n- Up to four star layers sit on top of each other, so the issue's \"different number of stars backgrounds\" can be combined, for example a slow layer of small dots under a fast warp of sparkles.\n- The stars and beams code is loaded with `import()` only when that layer is on ([`src/components/Cosmos.jsx`](../../../src/components/Cosmos.jsx)), so the defaults do not download it.\n- `src/visuals/layers.test.jsx` checks each layer: options built from the settings, the shapes, and that strength 0 draws nothing.\n\n| Star shapes                                   | Four star layers                              | Warp                                        |\n| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Star shapes](screenshots/star-shapes.png)   | ![Star layers](screenshots/star-layers.png)   | ![Warp](screenshots/star-warp.png)          |\n\n| Beams                               | Grid: crosses                                  | Grid: dashes                                  | Grid: dots                               |\n| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| ![Beams](screenshots/beams.png)     | ![Crosses](screenshots/grid-crosses.png)       | ![Dashes](screenshots/grid-dashed.png)        | ![Dots](screenshots/grid-dots.png)       |\n\n| Colours of the universe                              | Light theme                                       |\n| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Universe colours](screenshots/universe-colours.png) | ![Background light](screenshots/background-light.png) |\n\n## 7. Futuristic frames: each corner on its own\n\n- Each of the four corners of a panel has its own **shape**: square, cut, tall cut, wide cut, round, scoop or notch. It also has its own **line**: none (the \"missing border\" of the old skin), gap, line, accent or bracket. A size applies to all corners.\n- The settings page shows a tile for every choice, drawn with the real shape and line in the current colours ([`src/pages/CornerTiles.jsx`](../../../src/pages/CornerTiles.jsx)).\n- **How it is drawn.** [`src/skins.frames.js`](../../../src/skins.frames.js) generates `src/skins.frames.css` with `npm run build:frames`. Each shape is a `clip-path: polygon(...)` corner (round and scoop are approximated by arcs of points). Each line is a gradient image placed in that corner. The attributes `data-future-corner-tl`, `-tr`, `-br` and `-bl` choose the rules. `src/skins.frames.test.jsx` fails if the stylesheet is not up to date with the generator, and checks the polygons of every shape.\n- **Why not CSS `corner-shape`.** `corner-shape` (keywords round, scoop, bevel, notch, square, squircle and `superellipse()`) does exactly this, but it is not Baseline. MDN marks it as limited availability, and only Chrome and Edge 139+ support it ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/corner-shape), [Smashing Magazine, March 2026](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2026/03/beyond-border-radius-css-corner-shape-property-ui/)). Polygons work in every browser today.\n\n| Tiles, dark                                               | Tiles, light                                                | A custom frame on the home page                       | Zoomed corners                                    |\n| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Tiles dark](screenshots/frames-corner-tiles-dark.png)   | ![Tiles light](screenshots/frames-corner-tiles-light.png)   | ![Custom home](screenshots/frames-custom-home.png)    | ![Zoom](screenshots/frames-custom-zoom.png)       |\n\n## 8. Sound design\n\n- **31 synthesized sounds.** 26 come from [konard/immortality](https://github.com/konard/immortality) (the Unlicense): freq, filter, quartz, cobalt, comet, ion, halo, tide, mica, nova, zephyr, ember, prism, glacier, pulsar, orbit, vapor, cinder, tungsten, helix, drift, basalt, flint, opal, lumen, sonar, vesper and relay. 5 are new: raindrop, link, glass, warp and byte. All are made with Web Audio oscillators, noise and filters, so there are no files to download ([`src/sound/library.js`](../../../src/sound/library.js)).\n- **Interactions.** Hover, click, toggle, slider, page change and the rest each have up to four slots, each with a sound and a level. The slots play at random, in turn, or together ([`src/sound/interactions.js`](../../../src/sound/interactions.js)).\n- **The whole mix.** Volume, tone, room echo and room size, pitch variation, and stereo towards the pointer.\n- **Controls.** A ▶ button for every sound. A sound switch in the top bar. Sound is off by default.\n- **Cost.** The sound code is loaded only when sound is on (`src/components/Sound.jsx`).\n\n**A click in mica (root cause).**\n\n- [`experiments/sound-render.mjs`](../../../experiments/sound-render.mjs) renders each sound offline and measures it ([`sound-levels.json`](sound-levels.json)). Mica had a peak 15 times higher than its body.\n- [`experiments/sound-isolate.mjs`](../../../experiments/sound-isolate.mjs) narrowed the peak down to the first sample.\n- The cause is that a `GainNode` starts at 1 and stays at 1 until its first scheduled event. One sample of full-scale noise got through before the envelope began.\n- [`src/sound/engine.js`](../../../src/sound/engine.js) now sets `amp.gain.value = 0` before scheduling, and `src/sound/sound.test.jsx` checks that every gain starts silent.\n\n| Sound settings, dark                                   | Light                                                    | Phone                                                      | Top bar, sound on                                |\n| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |\n| ![Sound dark](screenshots/sound-settings-dark.png)     | ![Sound light](screenshots/sound-settings-light.png)     | ![Sound 360](screenshots/sound-settings-360-dark.png)      | ![Top bar](screenshots/sound-topbar-on.png)      |\n\n\"All other configuration options from all previous issues\" (issue #13): the settings of the universe, grid, rain, motion, the three skins, the notation and the theme are all still there. `applied.test.js` checks that every one of them is used.\n\n## 9. Presets\n\n- **Built-in presets.** 9 looks: Default, Calm, Matrix, Deep space, Warp, Neon HUD, Liquid, Blueprint, and Light and fast. Each tile shows a miniature drawn from the preset's own settings, not a screenshot.\n- **Saved looks**, kept in this browser (`localStorage`):\n  - save, apply, update, rename and delete;\n  - copy as JSON and load in another browser;\n  - synced between tabs by the `storage` event.\n- **Random.** A random look is never heavier than the defaults: no more layers, stars or frames per second.\n- **Links.** A `#settings=` link carries the look. Opening it keeps the look it replaced as a saved look.\n- **What a look never changes:** motion (reduced motion is an accessibility choice), volume and notation.\n- **Cost.** `presets.js` is loaded with `import()` only on the settings page or with such a link.\n\n| Presets, dark                               | Light                                        | Matrix applied                               | Saved looks                                 | Phone                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Presets](screenshots/presets-dark.png)    | ![Light](screenshots/presets-light.png)      | ![Matrix](screenshots/presets-matrix.png)    | ![Saved](screenshots/presets-saved.png)     | ![Phone](screenshots/presets-360-dark.png)    |\n\n## 10. Fast on phones\n\n**Measurement.** [`experiments/perf-mobile.mjs`](../../../experiments/perf-mobile.mjs) opens each page in Chromium as a phone: 412×915, ×2.6, a CPU four times slower, and slow 4G. It runs 3 times, waits 6 s, and records:\n\n- the first contentful paint (FCP);\n- the total time of long tasks (each over 50 ms, as [web.dev](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-long-tasks) defines them);\n- the frames per second of the background;\n- the bytes transferred.\n\nThe results are in [`data/perf-mobile-main.json`](data/perf-mobile-main.json) and [`data/perf-mobile-branch.json`](data/perf-mobile-branch.json). They are medians.\n\n| Page        | FCP, main → branch (ms) | Long tasks, main → branch (ms) | Frames/s, main → branch | Transferred, main → branch (kB) |\n| ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------- |\n| `/`         | 2844 → 3056             | 5405 → 3359                    | 6 → 13                  | 204 → 217                       |\n| `/settings/`| 1788 → 2052             | 5293 → 2817                    | 6 → 16                  | 126 → 128                       |\n| `/art/`     | 2204 → 2416             | 5581 → 3005                    | 6 → 19                  | 168 → 161                       |\n| `/blog/`    | 2108 → 2064             | 5527 → 3830                    | 7 → 15                  | 142 → 135                       |\n| `/cv/`      | 1784 → 1864             | 5477 → 2836                    | 6 → 21                  | 135 → 150                       |\n\n**What costs the most.** The same script with one layer switched off at a time showed:\n\n- universe off: 25 frames/s and 903 ms of long tasks;\n- motion off: 28 frames/s;\n- rain, stars or blur off: no change.\n\nThe universe is a full-screen shader, so it is the layer to adapt.\n\n**The fixes.**\n\n- **The governor.** [`src/visuals/governor.js`](../../../src/visuals/governor.js) watches the gaps between animation frames. When most of the gaps in a window are over 45 ms, it first lowers the resolution of the universe (×0.7 per step, down to 40%), then halves its frames per second (down to 25%). Stars and beams only lower their frames per second, so the sprites stay sharp. It never goes above the settings, does not judge the first second, ignores gaps over 1 s (a hidden tab), and never comes back up, so a layer does not flicker between two sizes. `src/visuals/governor.test.js` covers it.\n- **Smaller shared code.** The chunk shared by every page carried the career data, because the home page imported the CV builder only to make the links to the CVs. [`src/cv/paths.js`](../../../src/cv/paths.js) now makes those links without the builder, and the Layout chunk went from 111.5 to 90.8 kB gzip.\n- **Lazy loading.** Stars, beams, sound and presets are loaded with `import()` only when used.\n\n**The result, stated plainly.** Long tasks are about 45% shorter and the background runs 2–3 times more frames per second. FCP did not improve: it is 80–260 ms later on four pages and 44 ms earlier on `/blog/`. The new settings add some JavaScript. The text is drawn by React after the scripts load, so FCP waits for them (see [section 14](#14-limits)).\n\n## 11. Every screen\n\n**The check.** [`experiments/responsive.mjs`](../../../experiments/responsive.mjs) runs 9 pages × 4 widths (360, 768, 1280, 1920) × 2 themes = 72 cases. For each case it checks that:\n\n- nothing scrolls sideways;\n- no element sticks out of the screen;\n- the link of the current page is visible in the top bar;\n- at least three page links are at least half visible.\n\nIt also saves the first screen of every page.\n\n- **main**: 8 of 72 fail ([`data/responsive-main.log`](data/responsive-main.log)). At 360 px, the home page, `/research/` and `/blog/` show only two page links, and `/research/` and `/blog/` hide the current page. At 768 px, `/blog/` hides the current page. Both themes fail the same way.\n- **this branch**: 72 of 72 pass ([`data/responsive-branch.log`](data/responsive-branch.log)).\n\n**The cause.** On a phone the brand, the page links and the switches shared one row, so the page list got about one and a half links of width. The list scrolled, but it started at the first link, so a page further down the list was out of sight.\n\n**The fixes.**\n\n- Below 720 px the page links get their own row of the top bar.\n- `centreCurrent()` scrolls the current page into the middle of the list ([`src/components/edges.js`](../../../src/components/edges.js)).\n- A list fades only at an edge that has more links behind it (`data-more=\"left right\"`, set on scroll and resize).\n- The section links of a page stay on phones; before, only the ↑ button was left.\n- The checkbox of the blog filter was stretched to the full width like the text inputs; now only the text inputs are.\n- `src/components/edges.test.js` tests the marks, the centring and the cleanup.\n\n| Top bar at 360 px: main (above) and this branch (below)                      | Blog filter at 360 px: main and this branch                                        |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![Top bar](screenshots/responsive/topbar-360-main-vs-branch.png)             | ![Blog filter](screenshots/responsive/blog-filter-360-main-vs-branch.png)          |\n\n| Home, 360, dark                                    | Home, 360, light                                    | Research, 360                                          | Settings, 768                                           |\n| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![](screenshots/responsive/home-360-dark.png)      | ![](screenshots/responsive/home-360-light.png)      | ![](screenshots/responsive/research-360-dark.png)      | ![](screenshots/responsive/settings-768-dark.png)       |\n\n| Home, 1280                                         | Home, 1920                                          |\n| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |\n| ![](screenshots/responsive/home-1280-dark.png)     | ![](screenshots/responsive/home-1920-dark.png)      |\n\n## 12. Libraries and research\n\n| Library or standard | What it does | Why it is not used here |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [augmented-ui](https://augmented-ui.com/docs/) (BSD-2) | Pure CSS cut corners and borders with 150+ custom properties | Very close to the frames of section 7. It is a whole styling system with its own markup (`data-augmented-ui`), and the shapes here also need round, scoop and per-corner lines with previews; 270 lines of generator gave exactly those. |\n| CSS [`corner-shape`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/corner-shape) | round, scoop, bevel, notch, squircle, superellipse() | Not Baseline (Chrome/Edge 139+ only). Polygons work everywhere; a later issue could switch when it is Baseline. |\n| [Arwes](https://github.com/spaceblocks/arwes), [docs](https://arwes.dev/docs) | Futuristic frames (`@arwes/frames`) and sounds (`@arwes/bleeps`) | Still alpha; its frames are SVG drawn by JavaScript per panel, heavier than CSS. Used as a reference for the look. |\n| [Tweakpane](https://tweakpane.github.io/docs/misc/) | A settings panel with `exportState()` / `importState()` | The idea of exporting a whole state is the same as the JSON of saved looks. The settings page is part of the site's design and translated (EN/RU), so it stays in React. |\n| [lil-gui](https://discourse.threejs.org/t/lib-why-changed-dat-gui-to-lil-gui/62124), Leva | Debug panels (lil-gui replaced dat.gui; Leva is for React) | Same as Tweakpane: a developer panel, not a page for visitors. |\n| [ZzFX](https://npmjs.com/package/zzfx) | Tiny (<1 kB) sound synth from parameter arrays | A good fit in size; the sounds of immortality were already written for Web Audio and are kept as they are, with their names. |\n| [Howler.js](https://howlerjs.com/) | Plays audio files (7 kB gzip) | There are no audio files: every sound is synthesized. |\n| [tsParticles](https://particles.js.org/guide/bundles) | Particles with shapes (star in slim, twinkle in full, a stars preset) | The slim bundle alone is larger than `stars.js`, and it has no grid beams, no link to the grid period, and no per-layer blending. |\n| [web.dev: long tasks](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-long-tasks) | A long task is over 50 ms | The measure used in section 10. |\n\n## 14. Limits\n\n- **FCP.** The pages are rendered by React in the browser, so the first paint waits for the scripts. Pre-rendering the HTML at build time (SSG) would make FCP independent of the scripts, but that is a change of the build of every page, not of the settings. The long tasks and the frames per second, which the settings do control, are better.\n- **The shader cost is measured in headless Chromium.** It draws with SwiftShader on the CPU, which overstates the cost of the universe compared with a phone's GPU. The numbers of section 10 compare main and this branch on the same setup, which is what they are for.\n- **`corner-shape`** is not used until it is Baseline (section 7).\n\n## 15. Reproduce\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnpm run check            # eslint, prettier, the 1500-line limit, secretlint\nnpm run test:ci          # vitest: settings applied, layers, frames, sound, presets, governor, edges\nnpm run build\nnpx vite preview --port 4173 &\nnode experiments/settings-layout.mjs                 # columns of the settings page per skin and browser\nnode experiments/responsive.mjs /tmp/responsive      # 9 pages × 4 widths × 2 themes\nnode experiments/perf-mobile.mjs                     # phone measurement (BASE=... for another server)\nnode experiments/sound-render.mjs                    # levels of every sound\nnode experiments/presets-e2e.mjs                     # presets, saved looks and links in a browser\nnode experiments/sound-e2e.mjs                       # sound switch, ▶ buttons and interactions in a browser\nnode experiments/corner-zoom.mjs                     # zoomed corners of every shape\n```\n\nTo compare with main, build main in a separate worktree, serve it on another port, and run the same scripts with `BASE=http://localhost:4174`.\n"
